findings.title: The Frontend's two board-to-board sockets have no pin-1 mark, so it can be plugged onto the FPGA-LDO board turned half a turn, putting 3.3 V and 5 V on signal pins.
findings.what: J1 and J2 (Hirose DF40C-70DS, 0.4 mm-pitch board-to-board receptacles on the bottom) have no silkscreen at all: their footprints carry only fabrication-layer outlines, their reference texts are hidden, and nothing else on the bottom marks them. The matching FPGA-LDO A headers do carry pin-1 arrows. The pair is symmetric under a 180 degree turn: turned, Frontend J1 pin 1 lands on FPGA-LDO J2 pin 70, so each pin n mates with pin 71-n and J1 and J2 swap; only 2 of the 140 contacts then carry the same net. Frontend VIN_3V3 (J2 pins 68-70) lands on FPGA-LDO J1 pins 3/2/1 (ASIC8_READ, BOARD3_CLK, ASIC6_DATA1), and VIN_5V (J1 pin 32) lands on ASIC3_DATA4; these FPGA-LDO lines go only to the ASIC sockets (and R21). The FPGA-LDO board's own 3.3 V contacts land on Frontend J1 pins 3/2/1, which are FPGA balls. Frontend ground lands on 13 FPGA-LDO signal contacts, and FPGA-LDO ground on 13 Frontend FPGA signal pins. In bring-up stage 3 of the user guide the Frontend is mated to the FPGA-LDO board with no ASIC boards fitted, so no ASIC stack is there to block a turned fit. The turned Frontend still lies inside the FPGA-LDO outline; whether its bottom parts would stop it seating fully was not checked. User guide section B2.2 warns only about the ASIC boards. The FPGA-LDO and ASIC boards carry pin-1 dots and outlines at their board-to-board pairs; the Frontend does not.
findings.consequence: A Frontend turned half a turn puts its 3.3 V and 5 V onto FPGA-LDO lines meant for 1.5 V ASIC signals and ties 13 FPGA signal pins to ground. It also leaves the FPGA-LDO board's 3.3 V fed only through three FPGA pins (U15, V17, V16), so its regulators try to start from FPGA pins. FPGA pins damaged this way could later harm the bonded ASICs once those are fitted.
findings.do: Add a pin-1 dot and a connector outline on the bottom silkscreen at J1 and J2, matching the FPGA-LDO A marks (no copper change). Name the Frontend's orientation in user guide sections B2.2 and B5 (stage 3).
findings.where: Frontend J1 (122.245, 112.57) and J2 (104.745, 112.57), bottom; pin 1 at (120.705, 119.37) and (103.205, 119.37). Mates FPGA-LDO A J1 (91.255, 127.0) and J2 (108.755, 127.0), top. Turned case: Frontend J2.68-70 VIN_3V3 -> FPGA-LDO J1.3/2/1; Frontend J1.32 VIN_5V -> FPGA-LDO J2.39.
findings.source: Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_pcb (Frontend 14 layers V13): J1/J2 footprints, bottom silkscreen and pad nets; FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V24.kicad_pcb: J1/J2 pin-1 marks and pad nets; system datasheet user guide B2.2 and B5; Hirose DF40 series, https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40

findings.title: Most ASIC lanes that change layer at J2 have no ground via stack nearby for their return current.
findings.what: At J2, 40 lanes run on L8 or L10 and drop to L14 through a buried via and laser vias. Their return current must move from the inner ground planes (L7, L9, L11) to L13, which needs a ground via stack (L2 to L13) close by. The J2 field has only one such stack, at (106.0, 104.4). 36 of the 40 lanes are more than 2 mm and 34 more than 3 mm from the nearest stack; the median is 5.0 mm and the worst 6.84 mm. On the J1 side the same check gives at most 1.85 mm. The project's routing rule G05 asks for a nearby ground return transition at each signal via. Across the board there are 683 ground vias but only 55 full L2-L13 ground stacks (one of them runs L1-L14), and the only through-hole ground pads are J3's four shield slots. The layer changes of the cable LVDS pairs, the transceiver reference clock and the 25 MHz clock each have a ground stack 0.42-1.13 mm away, so the long return paths are limited to the J2 field and the bottom capacitors (FE-21).
findings.consequence: The lanes, including the returned 32 MHz clocks and an SPI clock, share long return detours near the ASIC connector, which adds ground bounce and crosstalk. The lanes use slow slew, so a failure is unlikely, but a glitch cannot be ruled out without ASIC edge data.
findings.do: Add full ground via stacks (buried via plus lasers to L2 and L13) beside the J2 GND pins and in the J2 via rows where room allows, then repeat the distance check aiming for about 1-1.5 mm, as on the J1 side.
findings.where: Frontend J2 field, x 102.2-107.5 mm, y 104.4-121.9 mm. Worst: /ASIC5_DATA4 (103.02, 117.4) L10, 6.84 mm; /ASIC5_DATA2 6.60 mm; BOARD3_SPI_CLK L8 6.49 mm; /ASIC5_SYNC 6.45 mm.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file, via positions and spans (pcbnew); project routing ground rules V1, rule G05

findings.title: JLC has not accepted in writing the laser vias stacked up to six high and the 0.170 mm hole-to-copper gaps.
findings.what: The board has 2,774 vias and no through vias: 2,373 laser vias (0.10 mm hole, 0.25 mm land) and 401 buried L4-L11 vias (0.15/0.30 mm). 241 sites stack three laser vias on L1-L4 and 188 on L11-L14. Counting all laser vias stacked at one point, 226 sites have 3, 153 have 4, 23 have 5 and 29 have 6; the 29 six-high sites sit on a buried via and form full L1-L14 stacks. 606 laser vias sit directly on a buried via (276 on L3-L4, 330 on L11-L12); KiCad's co-located-hole warning lists only 71 of them, so DRC understates the stacking. JLC's HDI page supports stacked vias but gives no stack-height limit and prefers staggered vias. The laser hole and land, the 0.071 mm dielectric and the buried-via aspect ratio (about 6.4) are within JLC's HDI FAQ, and the closest holes of different nets are 0.247 mm apart against the project's 0.24 mm rule. Separately, at 199 places a via hole comes within 0.170-0.199 mm of copper of another net (DRC with a 0.20 mm hole-clearance rule: 199 violations on 182 vias and tracks, none below 0.170 mm, never next to a pour). JLC's HDI figure is 0.15 mm, but its general rigid-board table says 0.20 mm; the project rule is 0.15 mm, so the normal DRC does not flag these. In the 16 Nov cart the buried vias and laminations were 'manual quote', and the PCB remark box held only 178 characters of the order note. Eight questions on the HDI build, the stacked laser vias among them, went to JLC support by e-mail on 19 Nov 2026; there is no answer yet.
findings.consequence: JLC may re-quote, ask for changes or trim copper near holes during its engineering review, delaying the order. Stacks three to six high on capped buried vias are a known weak point for via reliability. Moving to staggered vias would mean re-routing the U1 field.
findings.do: Before paying, get JLC's written acceptance of these stacks on capped buried vias and of 0.170 mm hole-to-copper. Its answer to the 19 Nov 2026 e-mail is the place for it; if that e-mail did not carry the via counts (stacks of 3-6 lasers, 29 full L1-L14 stacks, 606 lasers on buried vias) and the 0.170 mm figure, send them too.
findings.where: Frontend U1 BGA field and the J1/J2 fan-out; tightest holes on inner layers (for example buried vias at x 115.02-115.82, y 109.40 on L4).
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (pcbnew via count; kicad-cli DRC with a 0.20 mm hole_clearance probe rule); JLCPCB HDI capabilities FAQ, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/hdi-pcb-capabilities-faq ; JLCPCB HDI page, https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb ; JLCPCB PCB capabilities, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities ; JLC test order record 16 Nov

findings.title: J3's shield tabs get only a top fillet of solder, and a bottom-side touch-up could bridge VIN_3V3 to ground.
findings.what: The four shield tabs of the Micro-HDMI receptacle J3 sit in plated slots and are soldered by paste printed on the top pads only (1.5 x 2.55 mm opening, about 0.17-0.20 mm3 of solder per slot against about 1.6 mm3 of slot volume). Molex draws the tabs 0.55 +/- 0.15 mm long, so on the 1.574 mm board they stop well short of the bottom. Each joint is therefore mainly a top fillet. The order note asks JLC to 'make sure all four are soldered', which could prompt a bottom touch-up; on the bottom the slot ring is 0.16 mm from C83 (VIN_3V3) and 0.18 mm from R27 (VCCAUX_1V8). The slot barrels are also tied solidly, with no thermal spokes, to all five inner ground planes (L2, L7, L9, L11, L13): every ground pour uses a solid pad connection and no design rule overrides it for J3. In reflow the whole board heats, so this barely changes the joints, but it makes hand touch-up or rework of J3 hard.
findings.consequence: The tab joints are J3's only anchor against cable forces; weak joints let plugging forces load the 0.4 mm-pitch signal joints. A bottom touch-up could short VIN_3V3 or VCCAUX_1V8 to ground. Reworking J3, the board's only cable connector, is difficult because the slots sink heat into five planes.
findings.do: Change the assembly note to ask for top-side solder only on the shield tabs, with no bottom touch-up. Pull-test J3 on one assembled board before relying on it. On a later layout, give the J3 shield pads 2-4 thermal spokes on the inner ground layers.
findings.where: Frontend J3 shield slots at (109.4, 98.28), (109.4, 101.64), (115.6, 98.28), (115.6, 101.64); bottom C83 pad 1 (VIN_3V3), R27 pad 1 (VCCAUX_1V8); ground pours on L2, L7, L9, L11, L13.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (J3 slot pads: F.Paste only; L14 gaps; ground pour pad connection and .kicad_dru rules); Frontend order note (assembly remark, J3 line); Molex SD-46765-001 drawing, https://www.lcsc.com/datasheet/C563878.pdf

findings.title: JLC has not said how it reads bottom-side angles or library angle offsets; a wrong reading would land up to nine polarised bottom parts turned half a turn.
findings.what: The placement file gives KiCad's own angle for bottom parts, and the order note says so and lists pin 1 for 22 parts. JLC publishes no bottom-side rule, while common tools (kicad-jlcpcb-tools, KiBot) write 180 minus the angle. Under that rule U5, U6, U10, U11, U14, Y1 and Y2 (CPL angle 0 or 180) would be turned 180 degrees. Their pads are symmetric, so they would solder down with supply and ground swapped. A second, separate risk: U8 (flash level shifter) and U15 (transceiver-enable translator) carry a +90 degree library offset in the placement file (U8 90 against KiCad's 0, U15 270 against 180; U11, U17 and U18 carry the same offset). The order note says the offsets are included but not how they apply to a mirrored bottom part; if JLC applies them with the opposite sign, U8 and U15 land turned 180 degrees. U8's GND (pin 8) would then sit on pad 16 (VCCO_1V5) and its VCCA (pin 14) on a GND pad; U15's GND (pin 2) would sit on pad 5 (VCCO_1V5). U17 and U18 are symmetric, so a half turn is harmless for them. The pin-1 table lists U8 and U15. Y1 and U7 have no silkscreen pin-1 mark; U12 has one short line. In the 16 Nov cart the bottom side 'looked aligned' in JLC's preview, but it was not checked part by part.
findings.consequence: A regulator, the load switch, a buffer or an oscillator is reverse-powered at first power-up; U5, U6 and U10 would short their input rail to ground. A reversed U8 or U15 shorts VCCO_1V5 through the part, stresses U4's output and leaves the board unable to boot from flash or start the transceiver rails.
findings.do: Keep 'confirm parts placement' on and, before production, check pin 1 of U5, U6, U8, U10, U11, U14, U15, Y1, Y2, U7 and U12 in JLC's placement preview against the pin-1 table; or get JLC's written rule for bottom-side angles and library offsets first.
findings.source: Frontend order files (CPL with library offsets on U1, U8, U11, U15, U17, U18; pin-1 table; JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt); kicad-jlcpcb-tools fabrication.py, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Bouni/kicad-jlcpcb-tools/main/fabrication.py ; KiBot position notes, https://kibot.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notes_position.html ; JLCPCB pick-and-place help, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/pick-place-file-for-pcb-assembly

findings.title: The order notes set the bottom stencil but not the top, where the 0201 parts and the five power modules also need a thin one.
findings.what: The assembly remark asks for a 0.08 mm stencil on the bottom side (or a step-down at U7) and an X-ray of the boot flash U7. It says nothing about the top side, so JLC chooses there among its 0.10, 0.12 and 0.15 mm stencils; its own guide suggests 0.12 mm for boards that mix 0603 parts and 0.5 mm-pitch ICs, as this one does. How well paste releases is judged by the area ratio (opening area divided by its wall area), against the IPC-7525 guideline of 0.66 (JLC's stencil guide allows about 0.60 for electropolished and 0.55 for nano-coated stencils). At 0.12 mm the top-side 0201 resistors and capacitors come to 0.60 and the five MPM3833C modules (U2, U3, U4, U13, U16) to 0.61; at 0.10 mm every top-side part passes.
findings.consequence: With a 0.12 mm top stencil the paste for the top-side 0201 parts and the power modules releases marginally, which raises the chance of starved joints.
findings.do: Add 'top stencil 0.10 mm' to the assembly remark, or ask JLC which thickness it will use on the top side.
findings.where: Frontend top side: the 0201 parts (for example R1, R4, R5, R41, R55, R59) and the MPM3833C modules U2, U3, U4, U13, U16; order_frame_V3/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt, 'U7 solder paste' line.
findings.source: Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_pcb paste layers and the paste Gerbers (Frontend_14L_V13_Test_Frame_V3_Gerbers.zip); Frontend order notes (order_frame_V3/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt); IPC-7525B stencil design guideline (area ratio 0.66)

findings.title: Many schematic notes and part fields are out of date; two notes still give the old enable source for the 1.5 V regulator U4.
findings.what: Power notes: the U2 note says 'PG_CORE_1V0 enables U3, U4 and U10' and the U3 note says U4 'follows core PG', but in schematic V57 U4 is enabled by U3's power-good (PG, net PG_AUX_1V8) and PG_CORE_1V0 reaches only U3 and U10 (the U3 note's first item and the U4 note are correct). The U2 note gives VCCINT_1V0 186.39 uF of output capacitance; with C4 not fitted it is 86.39 uF, as the core-bypass note on the same sheet says. The U15 note takes U13's enable limits from the MPM3834C data sheet (Rev 1.01 p.4), and the U16 note's main citation is still the MPM3834C, while every fitted module is an MPM3833C; the U3, U4 and U13 notes also keep an older MPM3834C link ahead of their MPM3833C paragraphs. Part fields: 158 parts say 'V63 schematic candidate ... no V63 PCB' although this is schematic V57 with a routed board, and others still say 'layout pending'. L3 is called a '1.5 V filter' but is fed from VCCAUX_1V8 (Y2 runs at 1.8 V). C88 cites a SiTime table, and the Y2 note opens with the old SiTime part and still names a 33 Ohm R44 where 150 Ohm is fitted. Y2 is the YXC OT201625MJBA4SL, and its datasheet link is a generic YXC family sheet with no ordering-code table, so its stability and temperature codes cannot be checked from it. Manufacturer is blank on U1, U5, U6, J3, R46, R47 and R48, and the MPNs (maker part numbers) of R8 and Y1 differ from the ordered parts (suffix or packaging variants). The TP1-TP13 test-point note counts 13 pads and leaves out TP14 (VIN_5V). Sheet: the on-sheet revision history stops at V48, with nothing for V49-V57 (including the V52/V53 power-sequencing changes). Citations: the U12 supervisor cites only the bare TI link, with no document number, revision or page, and the U11 buffer cites the bare Nexperia link the same way.
findings.consequence: No electrical effect, and the order BOM groups correctly by JLC number. But anyone bringing up or debugging the power sequence from the schematic would expect VCCO_1V5 to start on the core PG instead of VCCAUX's; the wrong capacitance figure misstates the rail FE-01 assesses; and a BOM built from the MPN or Manufacturer columns for another assembler would be incomplete or name other parts. The sheet also breaks the project's rule that each schematic citation gives document number, revision and page.

Make one text-only pass at the next schematic edit (no netlist change):
- Set the U2 note to 'PG_CORE_1V0 enables U3 and U10' and the U3 note to 'U4 follows U3 PG (PG_AUX_1V8)'.
- Correct the VCCINT figure to 86.39 uF.
- Cite the MPM3833C (Rev 1.0) for U13's enable limits and in the U16 note.
- Remove or correct the 'V63' and 'layout pending' texts.
- Describe L3 as the 1.8 V filter for Y2. Cite the YXC sheet for C88 and Y2, or note that Y2's stability code is unverified. Correct the R44 value in the Y2 note.
- Fill Manufacturer and set each MPN to the ordered part.
- Count TP1-TP14.
- Add V49-V57 to the revision history.
- Cite TI SLVSD65A for U12 and the Nexperia 74AUP2G07 data sheet for U11, each with its revision and the page or table used. Check those numbers against the documents before writing them in.

findings.title: The board-only Frontend KiCad download has no 3D models, and in the test-frame project eleven parts still do not show, so the stack-fit check cannot be repeated from the files.
findings.what: In the board-only project and its KiCad ZIP, 158 of the 162 3D-model links point to a project '3dmodels' folder that is not there (56 files, no model files); only U14, U15, U17 and U18 resolve, through KiCad's own library. The test-frame project and its ZIP carry that folder with 17 model files, and there 158 of the 169 fitted parts render. findings.title: The FCS_B pull-up R19 is 4.99 kOhm where AMD asks for 4.7 kOhm or less, and the U5 power-good pull-up is below TI's 10 kOhm minimum.
findings.what: AMD asks for a pull-up of 4.7 kOhm or less on FCS_B (to VCCO_14); R19 is 4.99 kOhm. The PROGRAM_B and INIT_B pull-ups R17 and R18 are 4.7 kOhm, as AMD asks. TI asks for a 10 kOhm to 1 MOhm pull-up on the TPS74801 power-good pin, which sinks at most 1 mA; R9 on BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 is 4.99 kOhm and sinks about 0.66 mA when pulled low. Neither is expected to fail.
findings.consequence: A slightly weaker configuration pull-up than AMD specifies, and a power-good pull-up outside TI's stated range; the board does not follow two data sheets it cites.
findings.do: At the next schematic edit, change R19 to 4.7 kOhm 0201 (same footprint, no copper change). Changing R9 to 10 kOhm is optional.
findings.where: Frontend: R19 (bottom) VCCO_1V5 -> FPGA_QSPI_CS_N (FCS_B); R9 (top) VIN_3V3 -> BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 (U5.3, U4.12, U6.5, U12.3). Both RC0201FR-074K99L.

findings.title: Two MPM3833C rails carry more output capacitance than the 100 uF maximum MPS lists, and all four use a feed-forward capacitor MPS does not show.
findings.what: MPS lists 10/22/100 uF minimum/typical/maximum output capacitance for the MPM3833C, tested at one point (1.2 V, 2 A, engineering samples). Fitted nominal values: VCCINT_1V0 86 uF, VCCAUX_1V8 97 uF, VCCO_1V5 113 uF, and VIN_3V3 (U16) 164 uF on the Frontend plus 44 uF behind U10 and the FPGA-LDO board's capacitors. DC-bias loss lowers the real values. U2, U3 and U4 also have a 22 pF capacitor from output to FB (C3, C14, C23) that the MPS circuit does not have.
findings.consequence: A rail could ring or oscillate on load steps once the FPGA design runs. Start-up is not at risk.
findings.do: On the first board, check ripple and a load step on VCCINT_1V0, VCCO_1V5 and VIN_3V3; or ask MPS to confirm these values.
findings.where: Frontend U2 (VCCINT_1V0), U3 (VCCAUX_1V8), U4 (VCCO_1V5), U16 (VIN_3V3); C3, C14, C23.
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist (C4, C59, C89 not fitted); MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0 p.5 converter system table, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/713/MPM3833C_r1.0.pdf

findings.title: At the worst-case head load the 5 V input comes close to the HDMI port's 0.637 A current limit.
findings.what: All Frontend and FPGA-LDO power enters on one cable contact, J3.19 (VIN_5V), and passes through U16. Each HDMI Extension Board port switch (TPS2553, R711-R718 = 37.4 kOhm) limits at 0.637 A minimum. The system datasheet puts the head at about 0.32 A typical and 0.68 A worst case at 3.3 V, about 0.53 A at 5 V, which the chosen 3 ft cable can deliver (about 0.74-0.78 A at 3.3 V). The margin in the worst case is about 0.1 A, and the FPGA-LDO board's start-up surge adds briefly to it. U16 is a buck converter, so if its input sags it draws more current.
findings.consequence: In the worst case (all stimulators on) a port could reach its current limit and the stack could brown out or fail to start.
findings.do: On the first Frontend + FPGA-LDO stack, measure VIN_5V at TP14 at full load and during start-up.
findings.where: Frontend J3.19 VIN_5V, TP14, U16 -> VIN_3V3 (also to the FPGA-LDO board on J2 pins 68-70); HDMI Extension Board U701-U708, R711-R718.
findings.source: System datasheet V1 sections on head power and cable (2026-11-16_FPGA_Work/01_System_Datasheet_V1); TI TPS2553 data sheet, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf

findings.title: With the older regulator chip, MGTAVCC can reach 1.035 V in the worst case, 5 mV above AMD's 1.03 V; measure it on the first board.
findings.what: U5 sets the 1.0 V transceiver supply MGTAVCC with R10 (1.3 kOhm, 1 %) over R11 (4.99 kOhm, 0.1 %), 1.008 V nominal. U5 and U6 are TPS74801DRCR, which TI ships with either of two chips: the older one is accurate to 2 %, the new one to 1 %. With both resistor tolerances, a 60 C rise and the feedback pin current all taken in the worst direction, MGTAVCC is 0.982-1.035 V with the older chip and 0.993-1.024 V with the new one. AMD's operating range is 0.97-1.03 V and the absolute maximum is 1.1 V. The order notes ask JLC which chip is on the reel.
findings.consequence: A board with an older-chip U5, resistors at their limits and a warm board could run MGTAVCC a few millivolts above AMD's operating range, still far below the 1.1 V absolute maximum.
findings.do: Measure MGTAVCC at TP7 on the first board, cold and warm, and note the chip code JLC reports for U5 and U6 (DLN or RFB).
findings.where: Frontend U5 (TPS74801DRCR, bottom), R10/R11 on Net-(U5-FB), MGTAVCC_1V0, TP7 (top).
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist and U5 note box; TI TPS748 data sheet SBVS074N p.6 (accuracy legacy 2 %, new 1 %), p.33 (M3 suffix), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps74801.pdf; AMD DS181 Table 1 and Table 2 (MGTAVCC 1.1 V absolute maximum; 0.97-1.03 V operating), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet

findings.title: The four MPM3833C modules use 0603 input capacitors and have no added SW copper, against the maker's layout guide.
findings.what: MPS asks for an 0805 ceramic input capacitor as close to the pins as possible and for added copper on SW for heat. U2, U3, U4 and U13 use 22 uF 0603 parts (C1, C12, C21, C85) about 1.8 mm from the IN pins, and their SW pads have no tracks or pours. U16 uses 0805 parts. The direct capacitor-to-IN/PGND connection is in place.
findings.consequence: Somewhat more input ripple and less thermal margin than the data sheet figures; small at the expected sub-amp loads.
findings.do: Check module temperature and VIN_3V3 ripple on the first board. Where room allows on a later layout, use the 0805 22 uF part and add a small SW copper patch.
findings.where: Frontend top: U2/C1, U3/C12, U4/C21, U13/C85 (GRM188R60J226, 0603); SW pads 5 and 15.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (pad distances, SW nets without copper); MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0 p.16, PCB layout guidelines 1-3, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/713/MPM3833C_r1.0.pdf

findings.title: MGTAVTT power-good is not used, so FPGA configuration can start without MGTAVTT confirmed good.
findings.what: U6's PG pin is unconnected and U6 is enabled by BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3, the same node that starts U12's reset delay. Configuration waits for VCCO_1V5 and MGTAVCC but not for MGTAVTT; it relies on U12's delay being much longer than U6's soft-start (about 15-18 ms with C50 10 nF).
findings.consequence: A slow or failed MGTAVTT would give a configured FPGA with badly calibrated transceiver termination instead of an FPGA held in reset.
findings.do: Nothing for a first build; on a later edit, join U6 PG to BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3.
findings.where: Frontend U6 pin 3 (PG) unconnected; U6 pin 5 EN on BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3; U12 pin 3; C84 on U12 CT.
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist; TI TPS748 SBVS074N, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps74801.pdf; AMD UG482, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug482_7Series_GTP_Transceivers

findings.title: A few small parts and the XADC supply lack the nearby bypass capacitor their makers show.
findings.what: U8's 1.8 V supply pin has its nearest capacitor 2.8 mm away; Y1 (125 MHz) reaches C81 about 3 mm away; U14 and U15's 1.5 V pins are about 3.9 mm from a capacitor. VCCADC_1V8 has only C57 (470 nF), where AMD shows 100 nF plus 470 nF. VCCO_1V5 has eleven 0.47 uF capacitors where AMD lists twelve for three banks, but it also has a 1 uF and two 100 nF.
findings.consequence: Small: slightly more supply noise at U8 and Y1 and slightly lower XADC accuracy. Nothing is expected to fail.
findings.do: On a later layout, add 100 nF 0201 parts at U8 pin 13, Y1 pin 6 and beside C57 where room allows.
findings.where: Frontend bottom: U8 pin 13 (C19, 2.8 mm); Y1 pin 6 (C81); U14 pin 6 (C34); U15 pin 1 (C27); VCCADC_1V8 = C57, L1, U1.J10.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file and schematic V57 netlist; AMD UG480 p.15, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug480_7Series_XADC ; AMD UG483 Table 2-2, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug483_7Series_PCB

findings.title: The U12 supervisor trips only below the minimum voltage of VCCAUX and the boot flash, so it works as a start-up timer, not a brown-out monitor.
findings.what: U12 (TI TPS389001) watches VCCAUX_1V8 through R45 (4.64 kOhm) and R46 (10 kOhm, both 0.1 %), a ratio of 1.464. Its thresholds are 1.15 V falling and 1.157 V rising (+/-1 %), so it asserts reset at VCCAUX of about 1.684 V (1.667-1.700 V) and releases at about 1.694 V (1.677-1.711 V). AMD recommends VCCAUX of at least 1.71 V, and the W25Q128JW flash U7 on the same rail needs at least 1.70 V. The U12 note describes its job as sensing the actual 1.8 V of VCCAUX, bank 0 and the flash. At power-up this makes no difference, because U3 has already regulated to 1.77 V or more before U12's 1.07 s delay ends.
findings.consequence: A VCCAUX dip into roughly 1.67-1.71 V, below the FPGA's and the flash's minimum, would not pull BOOT_RESET_N low, so the FPGA and flash could run out of specification without a restart. This is a brown-out coverage gap only.
findings.do: Decide what U12 is for. If brown-out detection matters, change R45 to about 4.99 kOhm (R46 kept at 10 kOhm), which moves the trip to about 1.72 V falling and 1.73 V rising, still below U3's lowest output of about 1.77 V; otherwise record in the U12 note that it is a power-up timer.
findings.where: Frontend U12 (TPS389001) pin 1 SENSE on FLASH_READY_SENSE; R45 (VCCAUX_1V8 to SENSE), R46 (SENSE to GND); U12 pin 6 BOOT_RESET_N -> U11 -> FPGA_PROGRAM_B, FPGA_INIT_B; U7 pin 8 on VCCAUX_1V8.
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist; TI TPS3890 data sheet SLVSD65A, device comparison table and electrical characteristics, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps3890.pdf ; AMD DS181 Table 2 (VCCAUX recommended minimum), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet ; Winbond W25Q128JW data sheet (VCC minimum 1.70 V)

findings.title: The XADC supply filter and the bank bypass capacitors are drawn apart from the FPGA and joined to it only by labels.
findings.what: The XADC is the FPGA's built-in analog-to-digital converter. Its filter parts L1 (VCCAUX_1V8 to VCCADC_1V8), L2 (GND to GNDADC_XADC), C57 and C58 form an island joined to the FPGA's XADC pins (J10, J9, K9, K10, L9, L10) only by the labels VCCADC_1V8 and GNDADC_XADC. C24-C40, C42, C101 and C107 hang on local VCCO_1V5/GND label buses away from the FPGA's VCCO pins. In all, 25 of the 149 passives (these 24 and R63) have no wire to any IC, connector or oscillator pin; the other support parts checked (pull-ups, feedback dividers, soft-start and delay capacitors) are wired to their pins. The netlist is correct.
findings.consequence: Readability only: a reader cannot see which pins these parts serve, and the XADC group breaks the project's rule that support parts are wired visibly to the pins they serve (the bank bypass groups are borderline, as a shared local rail bus). No electrical effect.
findings.do: When the sheet is next edited, draw L1, L2, C57 and C58 wired to the FPGA's XADC pins (VCCADC J10, GNDADC J9) and bring the bank bypass groups next to the VCCO pins they serve; keep labels for links between blocks only, and check that the netlist is unchanged.
findings.where: Schematic V57: XADC note box (1187, 1142) with L1, L2, C57, C58; bank bypass note box (757, 932) with C24-C40, C42, C101, C107.
findings.source: Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_sch wire geometry checked against the kicad-cli netlist; project rule 'Visible schematic connections'; AMD UG480 p.15 (XADC supply filter), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug480_7Series_XADC

findings.title: Bottom decoupling capacitors under the FPGA reach the main ground planes only through L13, a median 1.6 mm from a ground via stack.
findings.what: Each bottom capacitor's ground pad has a laser via to L13 only. L13 joins the other ground planes through 55 full ground via stacks, so the current runs sideways on L13. Of 54 bottom capacitors on FPGA rails, 45 have their ground pad more than 1 mm from a stack; the median is 1.6 mm. Worst: C55 (MGTAVTT) 3.86 mm, C54/C56 3.20 mm, C52 (MGTAVCC) 2.96 mm, C18 (VCCAUX) 2.85 mm.
findings.consequence: A little more loop inductance per capacitor (well under 1 nH), so slightly more supply noise at high frequency, most relevant on the transceiver supplies.
findings.do: Check transceiver link margin at bring-up. On a later layout, give the MGTAVCC/MGTAVTT capacitors (C51-C56) their own nearby ground stack.
findings.where: Frontend bottom under U1: C51-C56, C49, C18 and others.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (pcbnew: capacitor ground pads vs full GND via stacks); AMD UG483 chapter 2, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug483_7Series_PCB

findings.title: Short slow-signal tracks cut narrow slots in the L2 and L13 ground planes that some lanes and the 25 MHz clock cross.
findings.what: 38 short tracks on L2 and 37 on L13 (about 18 mm each layer) cut slots in those ground pours. Ten L12 lanes cross an L13 slot for 0.25-0.51 mm, including CLK25_PL (0.30 mm) and /ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out (0.25 mm); L11 is whole above them. A few L1 tracks cross L2 slots for 0.18-0.30 mm (/ASIC8_DATA2, BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3, FPGA_JTAG_TDI).
findings.consequence: Small local impedance bumps and a little extra crosstalk; the 25 MHz clock is where it matters most.
findings.do: On a later layout, move the CLK25_PL crossing off the L13 slot; leave the rest.
findings.where: Frontend L12 over L13: /ASIC5_DATA5 0.51 mm, CHIP_RESET_SHARED 0.46 mm, /ASIC3_DATA6 0.44 mm, CLK25_PL near (117.2, 116.1) 0.30 mm.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (filled zones, track sampling every 0.01 mm); project routing ground rules V1, G05

findings.title: JTAG TDI on L5 runs 10.9 mm over the MGTAVCC pour, so its return current flows in the transceiver supply.
findings.what: L5 is a signal layer whose nearest plane is the split L4 power layer. FPGA_JTAG_TDI runs 10.9 mm over the MGTAVCC_1V0 pour; other L5 nets (INIT_B, EN_GTPWR_3V3, BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3) also run over several supply pours.
findings.consequence: A small amount of noise enters MGTAVCC while JTAG is active, for example during in-system debug with the transceiver running.
findings.do: Avoid heavy JTAG traffic while measuring transceiver margin; on a later layout, keep TDI over VCCAUX or GND.
findings.where: Frontend L5: FPGA_JTAG_TDI over MGTAVCC_1V0 10.9 mm and VCCAUX_1V8 5.1 mm.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (L4 fill under each L5 track, pcbnew); engineering judgement

findings.title: The cable LVDS pairs are about 87-92 Ohm instead of 100 Ohm, and the order sets no impedance target for them.
findings.what: The six cable-pair tracks are 0.08 mm wide with a 0.31 mm gap on L8 and L10 between ground planes. On this stack-up that gives about 87 Ohm (L8) and 90-92 Ohm (L10) differential. The order note asks JLC only to report the impedance of these pairs; the cart has 'no impedance requirement'.
findings.consequence: About a 5 % reflection, harmless over 25 mm at these rates with correct termination. Ordering 'controlled 100 Ohm' on this copper would put it at the edge of JLC's +/-10 % window.
findings.do: Keep impedance control off for these pairs (or state about 90 Ohm as their target); do not order 'controlled 100 Ohm' on this copper. The 100 Ohm request in the order notes is for the GT pair on L1 only.
findings.where: Frontend /CABLE_CLK_P/N on L8 (25.3 mm), /CABLE_CMDSYNC_P/N on L10 (23.7-24.1 mm), /CABLE_SYNC_P/N on L8 (6.4 mm).
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (track widths, stack-up L7-L11); analytic edge-coupled stripline calculation; JLCPCB HDI page (impedance +/-10 %), https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb

findings.title: At a low VCCO_1V5 and a high XEM LVDS level, the cable inputs keep only about 24 mV under AMD's recommended input limit.
findings.what: The cable LVDS pairs enter FPGA banks powered from VCCO_1V5. AMD recommends inputs stay below VCCO + 0.2 V. U4's worst-case low output is about 1.476 V (FB 591 mV, R7 150 kOhm / R8 100 kOhm, 0.1 %), so the limit is about 1.676 V; the XEM's worst-case high level is about 1.652 V. Typical parts leave about 0.3 V.
findings.consequence: Only a unit at both worst-case corners sits near the recommended limit; no damage is expected.
findings.do: At bring-up, measure the LVDS high level at R61/R62/R64 against VCCO_1V5.
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist; MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0 p.4 (VFB 591-609 mV), https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/713/MPM3833C_r1.0.pdf; AMD DS181 Table 2, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet

findings.title: The ASIC's input and output voltage figures are not on record, though the ASIC designer confirmed 1.5 V Schmitt-trigger logic.
findings.what: Every ASIC-facing FPGA pin uses LVCMOS15 on VCCO_1V5, matching the ASIC's 1.5 V digital supply. The ASIC designer said the chip uses 1.5 V logic with Schmitt-trigger inputs and edges no faster than about 1 ns, but gave no VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL figures.
findings.consequence: If the ASIC switches at an unusual fraction of its supply, data errors are possible; unlikely given the designer's answer.
findings.do: Ask the ASIC designer for the input and output levels at 1.5 V when convenient; confirm data integrity at bring-up.
findings.where: Frontend U1 banks 14, 15, 34 on VCCO_1V5; ASIC lines on J1/J2.
findings.source: Frontend pin file (LVCMOS15); ASIC reference (2026-10-04_FPGA_Work/08_ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md, item U03); AMD DS181 Table 8, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet

findings.title: Y2's data sheet covers only a 15 pF load, so its drive into the 830 Ohm level-shift divider is not specified.
findings.what: The 25 MHz oscillator Y2 drives R44 (150 Ohm) and R63 (680 Ohm) to ground to bring its 1.8 V swing down to about 1.47 V for the 1.5 V bank. The maker gives no output current or resistance; the divider draws about 2 mA. The FPGA still reads a high level if Y2's output resistance is below about 370 Ohm, which a normal CMOS output meets easily.
findings.consequence: Probably none; the operating point relies on an unpublished output characteristic.
findings.do: At bring-up, measure the CLK25_PL high level (expect about 1.4-1.5 V).
findings.where: Frontend Y2 pin 3 /CLK25_RAW -> R44 -> CLK25_PL (U1.T14) -> R63 -> GND.
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist; YXC oscillator data sheet, https://www.lcsc.com/datasheet/C669080.pdf

findings.title: Two footprint fixes exist only in the board file, so a library update would undo them.
findings.what: The board copy of J3 has top paste on its four shield slots and the board copy of U8 has a 0 mm solder-mask margin; the project library still has no slot paste for J3 and a 0.05 mm margin for U8. 'Update footprints from library' would silently revert both.
findings.consequence: A later revision could lose the J3 shield paste and bring back a thin mask web at U8. The current order files are not affected.
findings.do: Copy both changes into the project library footprints, or keep J3 and U8 out of library updates.
findings.where: Frontend J3 (Molex_MicroHDMI_46765_1xxx) and U8 (TI_RSV_UQFN16) in LearningFPGA.pretty.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file vs project library LearningFPGA.pretty

findings.title: U5, U6, U17, U18, R44 and R63 use generic land patterns that differ from the makers' examples.
findings.what: U5/U6 (TPS74801) pads are 0.85 x 0.28 mm, longer than TI's 0.6 x 0.24 mm example, leaving a smaller gap. U17/U18 (TPD4E02B04) use 0.30 mm for all ten lands where TI uses 0.20 mm signal lands and 0.40 mm GND lands. R44/R63 use KiCad's generic 0201 land (0.46 x 0.40 mm, 0.18 mm gap) unlike the board's other 0201 resistors.
findings.consequence: Slightly higher risk of solder bridging or tombstoning at assembly; no electrical effect.
findings.do: Check these joints at first-article inspection; switch to the makers' land patterns at the next footprint clean-up.
findings.where: Frontend U5, U6, U17, U18, R44, R63.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (pad sizes); TI TPS748 SBVS074N land example, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps74801.pdf; TI TPD4E02B04 data sheet, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpd4e02b04.pdf

findings.title: The not-fitted capacitors C4, C59 and C89 have paste openings, so their bare pads get solder bumps.
findings.what: C4, C59 and C89 are not fitted and are left out of the placement file, but their pads keep bottom paste openings. The order note asks JLC to leave the pads empty but not to block the stencil openings.
findings.consequence: Pre-tinned pads (handy for later hand-fitting) and a possible loose solder ball; otherwise harmless.
findings.do: Accept it, or ask JLC to block those six stencil openings.
findings.where: Frontend bottom: C4, C59, C89 pads.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (B.Paste on the pads); Frontend order note (assembly remark)

findings.title: A loose Frontend carries no board name, revision or reference designators.
findings.what: The board has no text on silkscreen or copper and none of its 218 reference designators is shown. The test frame names the board and its revision, but once broken out a board cannot be matched to its files by eye.
findings.consequence: Boards of different revisions can be mixed up at bring-up or repair, for example loading the wrong pin file.
findings.do: Mark each board when it leaves the frame (label or marker), or add a short name and revision text on a later layout.
findings.where: Frontend top and bottom silkscreen.
findings.source: Frontend PCB file (no board texts outside User.Comments; 0 visible references); Frontend order note (silkscreen line)

findings.title: The FPGA is the commercial 0-85 C grade, and no estimate shows its junction stays below 85 C in the head stack.
findings.what: The order places XC7A35T-2CSG325C (C1521720), junction limit 85 C. The 22.6 x 25.4 mm board dissipates roughly 0.9 W typical and up to about 1.6 W in the high case, and its underside faces the FPGA-LDO board 1.5 mm away. No Vivado power estimate or measurement exists.
findings.consequence: In the high case or a warm environment the FPGA could run past 85 C, with timing drift.
findings.do: Get a Vivado power estimate and read the FPGA's internal temperature (XADC) on the first stack under full load.
findings.where: Frontend U1 (top, 116.22, 113.0); regulators U2, U3, U4, U13, U16.
findings.source: Frontend order note (U1 C1521720) and BOM; AMD DS181 Table 2 (junction temperature by grade), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet

findings.title: JLC's bow and twist tolerance allows more warpage across J1/J2 than Hirose allows for the DF40 connectors.
findings.what: Hirose allows at most 0.02 mm of board warpage along a DF40 connector. JLC publishes 0.75 % bow and twist for HDI boards (0.5 % on request). On this 25.4 mm board, 0.75 % allows about 0.055 mm across the 13.6 mm contact span of J1/J2, and 0.5 % about 0.036 mm. The order note asks for 0.02 mm along J1/J2 and 0.5 %, but JLC has not agreed. The board's own copper imbalance (L3/L12, L7/L8, L6/L9) is calculated to add only a few micrometres.
findings.consequence: A board within JLC's tolerance can still solder J1/J2 with weak joints or mate unevenly.
findings.do: Inspect the J1/J2 joints (X-ray) and mate one stack on the first assembled boards before building more.
findings.where: Frontend J1 and J2 (DF40C-70DS, bottom).
findings.source: Hirose DF40 catalogue p.21 (board warpage), https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40 ; JLCPCB HDI page, https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb ; Frontend order note (flatness line)

findings.title: VIN_5V from the cable reaches U16 with no clamp, and hot-plug overshoot against its 6.5 V limit is unmeasured.
findings.what: The cable 5 V goes straight to U16's IN and EN pins and on to J1.32. The only parts on VIN_5V are C206, C207 (22 uF), C209 (100 nF) and TP14; there is no TVS. Plugging into a live port can ring above 5 V; U16's pins are rated 6.5 V absolute maximum.
findings.consequence: If the ringing is under-damped the peak could pass 6.5 V and damage U16, taking down every rail.
findings.do: On the first board, scope VIN_5V at TP14 while plugging the real cable into a live port.
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist; MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0 p.3 absolute maximum ratings, https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/713/MPM3833C_r1.0.pdf

findings.title: The DONE test point is on the bottom between J1 and J2, so it cannot be probed in a mated stack.
findings.what: TP12 (FPGA_DONE) and its pull-up R38 are on the bottom, facing the FPGA-LDO board when mated; the board has no LEDs. TP5 and TP9 both test VCCAUX_1V8.
findings.consequence: In a mated stack, configuration status can be read only over JTAG or from INIT_B (TP11). Bring-up of the Frontend alone is not affected.
findings.do: Check DONE before stacking, as the user guide does. On a later layout, TP9 could become FPGA_DONE.
findings.where: Frontend TP12 (bottom, 117.52, 110.20); R38 (bottom); TP5, TP9 (top, VCCAUX_1V8).
findings.source: Frontend PCB file and schematic V57 netlist

findings.title: A running XEM can drive the cable LVDS pairs into the Frontend before its 1.5 V I/O rail is up.
findings.what: The cable clock, command and SYNC pairs run from J3 straight to FPGA pins powered by VCCO_1V5. VCCO_1V5 comes up last (U16 -> U2 -> U3 -> U4) and is off whenever the port's 5 V switch is off. In that time the XEM can drive about 1.2 V into the unpowered bank through the FPGA's clamp diodes; AMD allows up to 10 mA per pin.
findings.consequence: Clamp current into the unpowered bank, probably within the 10 mA limit at LVDS levels but not quantified.
findings.do: In the XEM gateware, keep a port's LVDS outputs off until that port's 5 V is on and the Frontend has configured; or measure the clamp current on the first stack.
findings.where: Frontend J3 pins 6/8, 9/11, 12/14 -> U1 P14/R15, M14/N14, B9/A9; U4 EN = PG_AUX_1V8 from U3.
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist; AMD DS181 Table 2 (clamp current, powered or unpowered), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet

findings.title: The FPGA cannot be configured, even over JTAG, until the whole transceiver supply chain is up, and there is no jumper to bypass that during bring-up.
findings.what: U12 releases BOOT_RESET_N only when BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 is high, and that node is the joined power-good outputs of U4 (VCCO_1V5) and U5 (MGTAVCC). U5 is enabled only by U13's power-good, U13 only by EN_GTPWR_3V3 from the translator U15, and U15's 3.3 V side comes from the load switch U10. While BOOT_RESET_N is low, U11 holds PROGRAM_B and INIT_B low, which stalls configuration (AMD UG470 Table 2-4). This gating is deliberate (R9's part field describes it), although configuration itself is not expected to need the transceiver supplies (not confirmed in AMD's own documents). On the reset path the probe points are TP10 (BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3) and TP11 (INIT_B) on the top, and TP28 (BOOT_RESET_N) and TP35 (PROGRAM_B) on the bottom, which can be reached only while the board is not stacked. There is no jumper on U12's manual-reset input.
findings.consequence: A fault or missing part anywhere in U10, U15, U13, U5, R10 or the 1.4 V rail leaves the FPGA held in reset for good, so the board cannot be used to debug its own transceiver supply.
findings.do: At bring-up, if the FPGA stays unconfigured, check TP10, then TP3 (SWITCHED_3V3), TP16 (1V4_GTP_IN) and TP7 (MGTAVCC_1V0). EN_GTPWR_3V3 has no test pad and must be probed at U13 pin 4; its 1.5 V side, EN_GTPWR_1V5, is on TP45 (bottom). On a later revision, choose one of two options. One is to release configuration on VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCO only and watch the transceiver rails separately; this pulls against FE-34, which suggests adding MGTAVTT's power-good to the same gate, so decide the two together. The other is to add a not-fitted bring-up option that separates U12's manual-reset pin (MR, pin 3) from the power-good node and ties it to VIN_3V3. A plain 0 Ohm from that node to VIN_3V3 would short into the power-good outputs that pull it low.
findings.where: Frontend nets BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 (U4.12, U5.3, U6.5, U12.3 MR, R9, TP10), BOOT_RESET_N (U12.6, U11, U14, R47, TP28), FPGA_PROGRAM_B (U11.6, R17, TP35), FPGA_INIT_B (U11.4, R18, TP11); chain U10 SWITCHED_3V3 -> U15 -> EN_GTPWR_3V3 -> U13 -> PG_GTP_1V4 -> U5.

findings.title: On HDMI ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 the separate SYNC input floats, and the Frontend cannot tell which port it is on.
findings.what: Every Frontend feeds cable pins 12/14 (CABLE_SYNC) into an LVDS input (B9/A9) with only a 100 Ohm resistor (R64) and no bias. The HDMI Extension Board drives these pins only on ports 3-6. On the other ports the input sees 0 V between its legs and can read either level or toggle on noise.
findings.consequence: Gateware that uses CABLE_SYNC on ports 1, 2, 7 or 8 sees random sync pulses.
findings.do: Gateware must use the SYNC folded into the command line unless it knows it is on ports 3-6 (for example from a port number in the command stream).
findings.where: Frontend J3.12/J3.14 -> U18 -> R64 -> U1 B9/A9 (LVDS_25, DIFF_TERM FALSE).
findings.source: Frontend schematic V57 netlist and pin file; system datasheet V1, Frontend cable section; AMD DS181 LVDS input table, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet

findings.title: Bank 14 runs at 1.5 V while bank 0 runs at 1.8 V during configuration; Vivado has not been asked whether it accepts this.
findings.what: CFGBVS is tied to GND, so either 1.5 V or 1.8 V is allowed electrically. Bank 0 (CCLK) is on VCCAUX_1V8 and bank 14 (FCS_B, D00, D01) on VCCO_1V5; U8 translates to the 1.8 V flash. AMD's SPI table lists only matched bank voltages. The pin file sets CFGBVS GND and CONFIG_VOLTAGE 1.8.
findings.consequence: Probably no electrical problem; possibly a Vivado design-rule warning or error that needs to be understood.
findings.do: Run the pin file through Vivado once (synthesis, implementation, DRC, bitstream) and record the result.
findings.where: Frontend U1 E12 (CFGBVS) to GND; E10/R10 on VCCAUX_1V8; bank 14 on VCCO_1V5; U8 SN74AVC4T774.
